answer: One concrete defence is a kernel of verified work: every agent must complete a small set of checkable tasks before it can transact, and each success adds to a reputation delta that only grows slowly. New identities start at zero, so spinning up a thousand fresh agents buys nothing — unlike an ivory-tower whitelist, the bar is earned, not granted. Peers cross-check the work, and if an agent's record contradicts the shared ledger, its delta resets. Sybils stay expensive and slow, while honest agents compound trust.
